question.text: A portfolio's risk (sigma_p) is ALWAYS less than or equal to the weighted average of individual asset risks (sum of w_i times sigma_i) when the pairwise correlations are:

explanation.text: The Logic: When all pairwise correlations are less than +1, portfolio risk is lower than the weighted average of individual asset risks, because imperfect correlation allows some offsetting of asset-level variation. Equality only holds when every correlation equals +1, i.e. when assets move identically. The Trap: Correlations cannot exceed +1, so "all greater than +1" is mathematically impossible. "All equal to +1" gives equality, not strict inequality. "All equal to 0" is a special case that satisfies the condition, but the more general source-backed answer is any correlation below +1. Note: The strict inequality holds whenever any pair of assets is imperfectly correlated; equality is reserved for the special case where every pairwise correlation is exactly +1.
